newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka military columns link up in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka military columns link up in north.

text.p: Two divisions of government troops deployed to open a strategic highway in Sri Lanka's north have linked up, military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said on Thursday.

Troops of Operation "Jaya Sikuru" (Sure of Victory) which were mobilised against Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels had combined just south of Puliyankulam, Munasinghe told a news conference in Colombo.
Puliyankulam is some 22 km (14 miles) north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, on the 88 km (55 mile) highway from Vavuniya to Kilinochchi.
The link-up of the troops is seen as significant because once the area is captured it will open avenues for soldiers to advance in several directions against the LTTE, military officials say.
The troops, battling LTTE rebels in the northern Wanni region, joined up on Wednesday, Munasinghe said.

Military officials said one division of the army, backed by helicopter gunships, tanks and artillery had moved from Omanthai near Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, and had met the other division which had moved out from northeastern Nedunkeni.
"For the movement, we have achieved what we had planned to do. This does not mean that the operation is over. We will now consolidate and then move forward," Munasinghe said.
He declined to reveal the military's plans.
One soldier and four rebels were killed and 17 soldiers wounded in the fighting during the link-up, Munasinghe said.

Jaya Sikuru was launched in May. Fighting escalated last week as the LTTE launched a wave of counter-attacks. The military claimed a big victory in the battle, saying it had killed more than 200 rebels while losing 67 of its troops and police guarding defences.
The LTTE said they had lost 126 of their fighters in the attack.

The LTTE are fighting for a homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east in a war which began in 1983. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, but the LTTE put the toll higher.
